big: Two friends save ₹10,000 a month until 60. One starts at 25, the other at 35. At an assumed 10% a year, the first ends with about ₹3.8 crore and the second about ₹1.3 crore. Ten years made the gap.

lines: I am 35. Is it too late?
No. But the plan needs three things: start now, raise the amount as income grows, and check it once a year.

rows: Paid in over the years (₹ lakh)
alt: Two sets of bars comparing money paid in and the pot at sixty for two start ages
caps: Two friends, each saving ₹10,000 a month until sixty.
The early starter pays in ₹42 lakh over 35 years.
The later starter pays in ₹30 lakh over 25 years.
At an assumed 10%, the early start grows to about ₹3.8 crore against ₹1.3 crore.

h: A step-up SIP, assumed 10% a year
note: Returns are assumed to show the idea, and are not a forecast. Real returns vary, and can be lower.

q: Rohan is 30 and Meena is 40. Both want ₹2 crore at 60. Who needs the bigger monthly saving?
opts: Meena, since she has fewer years to grow the pot
Rohan, since young people save more per month
Neither, since the amount is the same
why: Fewer years of compounding means more must be put in each month.
Starting earlier lowers the monthly need, so Rohan needs less.
The target is the same, but the years to reach it are not.
Income does not decide it. The years left and the target do.

q: Meena's salary rises 10% each year, but her SIP stays at ₹10,000. What can she do?
opts: Stop her SIP until the pay doubles
Use a step-up SIP that rises each year
Move all her money to a savings account
Wait for a year without saving
why: Stopping loses years of compounding, which are hard to make up later.
A step-up SIP lifts the amount as income grows, adding to the pot over time.
A savings account usually grows slower than a long-term plan.
Waiting a year costs a year of growth she cannot get back.

q: Rohan is 55 and retires at 60. Why might he lower his share of equity now?
opts: Equity can never rise again after 55
Banks demand it after the age of 55 by rule
Safer assets always beat equity every year
A late fall leaves little time to recover
why: Equity can rise at any age, so that claim is not true.
No bank demands it. It is a choice made to manage risk.
Safer assets are steadier, but they do not always earn more.
A fall near retirement hits when he needs money and has little time to recover.

q: Which habit keeps a retirement plan on track?
opts: Looking at the plan only on retirement day
Changing the plan after every news headline
A yearly review of savings, returns and goals
Asking friends what their own plans are
why: A single look on the last day leaves no time for any changes.
Reacting to headlines leads to hasty changes and costs.
A yearly check lets her fix gaps early and adjust to changes in life.
A friend's plan suits a friend's life, not necessarily hers.

pts: Start early. Ten years of delay can cut the final pot by a lot.
A step-up SIP raises the amount as income grows.
Shift towards safer assets near retirement, and review once a year.
